label: early-prefix conjunction: w/i/l/p/m/g... after an early b/i/l (input steps 1-4)
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit (99.7% of mass): it never fires at t=0, peaks at t=2 (about half the mass), and covers t=1-4. It almost never fires on the delimiter or during copy. Whether it fires depends on a conjunction of the current input and the first few tokens. The current token is usually w (8.7x lift, 38% of mass), then i, l, p, m, g, q, s. The earlier prefix tokens are usually b, i, l (also g, m, 0). It is strongest on a w that comes right after b-i, b-l-i or b-b at t=2-3 (prefixes "b i w" and "b b w" give the max), and much weaker on a w after other prefixes. It favours first occurrences of a token. Position inside the 1-4 window and the timing alone predict poorly (precision 0.04), and no simple token set gets past F1 of about 0.39 on dev. It looks like a hashed code for particular early-prefix combinations rather than one clean concept.
